name: Survicate
summary: Customer feedback platform for continuous surveys: NPS, CSAT and in-product micro-surveys across web, in-app, email and link — with templates, audience targeting and native integrations (Segment and RudderStack among them) that pipe feedback straight into your CRM and analytics.
best_for: product and CX teams running always-on feedback — NPS, CSAT and in-app surveys — piped into the CRM and analytics stack they already use
skip_if: you just need an occasional one-off questionnaire (a simpler form tool covers that) or your response volume is huge — response-metered pricing punishes scale
honest_knock: The plan is metered by response volume, not by surveys — a viral NPS month can push you a tier up, and the free plan's 30-day retention quietly deletes your history. Mind the billing asymmetry too: Starter is monthly-only while Growth and up expect an annual commitment.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Growth (100 responses) · per month, billed annually
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-08 and re-read unchanged 2026-09-26 in the plan data embedded in survicate.com/pricing; from an EU exit the cards show EUR 99 for Growth at 250 responses, EUR 299 for Pro and EUR 499 for Enterprise) A 10-day trial of all features, no card. Growth is metered on feedback rather than seats and is a ladder, not a single price: $56 a month for 100 responses and 500 data points, $114 for 250 and 1,000, $169 for 500 and 1,500, $229 for 1,000 and 2,000, and $289 for 1,500 and 2,500 — billed annually, with 10 user seats across 2 teams and one dashboard at every rung. Pro is $349 with a custom yearly response pool, advanced survey logic and 10 dashboards; Enterprise is $569. Starter is monthly-only and has its own ladder with an explicit overage rate: $89 for 100 responses at $0.89 for each one beyond, $179 for 250 at $0.59, $279 for 500 at $0.39. A response is counted per respondent, partial or complete; data points are new external feedback from integrations (calls, tickets, reviews) and exclude survey responses.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Remote server over the whole feedback loop: list surveys and their questions, pull survey and per-question results (response and completion counts, answer distributions, NPS and CSAT) over a date range, search the responses, read and start AI research projects, and draft a survey that lands in the panel for review before launch. One-click OAuth, no API keys; every call runs as the connected user, so workspace role, folder access and Research Hub role apply as they do in the panel.
